calibration_notes: Stage 1 calibration reserves P1 for high-salience disclosures and keeps risk-factor-only mentions lower quality unless they contain concrete governance or deployment evidence.
Stage 2 calibration judges deployment and governance independently and uses insufficient_evidence when evidence is weak or generic.
Timeline calibration treats absent quarters explicitly; non-absent postures require linked evidence IDs.
All factors use higher_is_stronger to mean more disclosed AI involvement, maturity, or exposure; this is not a good/bad risk judgment.
known_limitations: Outputs are based on public/ingested disclosures and should not be interpreted as proof of undisclosed internal AI maturity.
Stage 1 and Stage 2 are precomputed for auditability; the frontend must not call Gemini at runtime.
Factor scores measure disclosed AI involvement, maturity, or exposure and are not standalone credit risk ratings.
Generic risk-factor mentions are retained with lower salience so sparse disclosure remains visible without overstating maturity.
Call Report or financial proxy trends may be unavailable for some banks and are explicitly marked as missing where absent.
Stage 2 review/failure file contains 55 low-confidence or insufficient-evidence review rows for audit follow-up.
232 bank-quarter timeline cells have no linked AI evidence and are explicitly marked absent.

quadrant_axis_definitions.deployment_stage.experimenting_piloting: Evidence shows pilots, experimentation, exploration, isolated use cases, early-stage implementation, limited rollout, or evaluation without clear scaled adoption.
quadrant_axis_definitions.deployment_stage.insufficient_evidence: Evidence does not support either scaled deployment or piloting; AI mentions are absent, generic, or risk-only.
quadrant_axis_definitions.deployment_stage.production_scaled: Evidence shows AI deployed in production, scaled across material workflows, or described as an enterprise capability.
quadrant_axis_definitions.governance_maturity.board_level: Evidence shows board, board committee, senior risk committee, proxy-governance, or formal enterprise oversight of AI.
quadrant_axis_definitions.governance_maturity.insufficient_evidenc: Evidence does not support a governance maturity classification.
quadrant_axis_definitions.governance_maturity.operational_ownershi: Evidence shows AI ownership by management, technology, compliance, model-risk, or business units without board-level oversight.

scoring_definitions.composite_score: No default composite AI ranking is exported. ai_scores.raw_score and peer_percentile satisfy the strict schema using the maximum individual factor value rather than a displayed composite.
scoring_definitions.direction_consistency: Higher factor values always mean more disclosed AI involvement, maturity, or exposure on that factor; they are not automatically good or bad risk judgments.
scoring_definitions.evidence_weighting: P1 evidence is weighted above P2 and P3; operational metrics and specific disclosures are weighted above generic mentions; high confidence is weighted above medium and low confidence.
scoring_definitions.factor.board_governance: Evidence of board, committee, director-level, proxy, or formal senior oversight of AI, model risk, data governance, technology, or responsible AI.
scoring_definitions.factor.compliance: Evidence of AI-related regulatory compliance, consumer compliance, fair lending, privacy, explainability, controls, or audit processes.
scoring_definitions.factor.growth_profitability: Evidence of productivity, efficiency, cost reduction, revenue growth, fraud savings, underwriting speed, or customer service improvements tied to AI.
scoring_definitions.factor.leadership_acumen: Evidence of senior management strategy, executive commentary, AI leadership, enterprise roadmaps, talent programs, or centers of excellence.
scoring_definitions.factor.risk_management: Evidence of model risk management, AI risk controls, validation, monitoring, data quality, cyber risk, or third-party risks related to AI.
scoring_definitions.factor.strategic_implementation: Evidence of AI deployment, pilots, production use, enterprise rollout, platforms, customer or employee workflow use, fraud detection, underwriting, servicing, or other operating use cases.
scoring_definitions.factor.strategic_risk: Evidence that AI changes strategic exposure, competitive positioning, operational resilience, reputation, vendor dependence, or business model risk.
scoring_definitions.placement_tier.P1: High-salience, specific AI disclosure in MD&A, CEO/shareholder letter, proxy governance, strategy discussion, or similarly central section.
scoring_definitions.placement_tier.P2: Specific AI disclosure in a less central section or with narrower operational context.
scoring_definitions.placement_tier.P3: Generic, risk-factor-only, or boilerplate AI disclosure retained for traceability but weighted lower.
